verified_findings: Typed constraints are enforced by a deterministic critic that directly projects, clips and scales proposed weights.
Raw mandate adherence is reported separately from post-critic feasibility. The system, not the constructor model, guarantees the executed constraints.
Audit artifacts distinguish PASS, FAIL and UNKNOWN contamination status; this is not a model-revision success rule.
not_supported: No model-feedback-rewrite iteration budget is established by these sections.
Projection success cannot demonstrate that the model used feedback or chose feasible raw weights.
Its position/name caps, cash buffer and trading assumptions are not imported into LIBERA.
papers.libera_transfer: Keep raw proposal, external check and acceptance status separate; reject its automatic projection for the current no-repair research question.

papers.citation: Yang et al. (2026), Precise but Uncoupled, arXiv:2607.15388v1
locators: Appendix I.1, Single-Agent Iterative and PER Reviewer
verified_findings: Detection, immediate candidate change and successful repair are distinct observations; answer change alone does not prove understanding.
Table 12 caps Single-Agent Iterative and PER at three outer attempts; PER has two inner rounds per attempt.
Prior candidate and failure advice are exposed; the PER reviewer instruction forbids approval after a failure indicator.
Mandatory verbal acknowledgment lowers FinalPassRate from 85.2% to 82.5%; embedding feedback reaches 86.3%, without uniformly improving all uptake diagnostics.
not_supported: The tested primary actor/evaluator is gpt-oss-120b on olympiad mathematics, not Qwen3.5-4B on financial allocation.
Three attempts is an experimental configuration, not a proven optimum for this task.
Acknowledgment is not evidence of repair, and direct presentation does not guarantee success.
The paper states code/data release awaits institutional approval; executable implementation parity is not independently established here.
papers.libera_transfer: Observe raw-vector change and recalculated feasibility separately. A bounded external arithmetic acceptance gate is a LIBERA adaptation; never supply evaluator-only labels or target weights.

papers.citation: Arimbur (2026), How Many Tries Does It Take?, arXiv:2604.10508v1
verified_findings: The next repair prompt contains the original specification, previous code and actual execution error; the model produces a new candidate and tests run again.
The main protocol allows four repair rounds after an initial attempt, five attempts total; prompt ablations use two repair rounds, three attempts total.
Greedy repair uses temperature zero. Model and task dependence, and the repair-versus-resampling decoding confound, are disclosed.
not_supported: The smallest evaluated model is Llama 3.1 8B; Qwen3 32B is not Qwen3.5-4B.
Code-test success is not portfolio strategy quality. Published repair gains and budgets are not validated LIBERA outcomes.
A repair prompt containing the previous candidate does not authorize dropping LIBERA's retained history.
papers.libera_transfer: Use the actual calculator error and unchanged task beside the prior raw proposal, ask the model to rewrite, then recompute; keep the original immutable.

locators: Algorithm 1, printed page 4 / PDF page index 3
Section 4.2, printed page 7 / PDF page index 6
verified_findings: Algorithm 1 alternates external-tool critique and model correction under a finite iteration parameter n and a stopping condition.
Its mathematical-program experiment permits four corrections and stops after two consecutive unchanged execution results; correction uses sampling p=0.5.
not_supported: Its stopping decision can use the critique rather than a sound arithmetic verifier.
Its correction sampling and task budgets are not silently substituted for the frozen LIBERA greedy runtime.
Returning the final candidate after the budget does not establish correctness or justify a success status.
papers.libera_transfer: Supports a finite verify-rewrite-verify pattern, with independent calculator acceptance and honest terminal failure added as explicit local design choices.

facts: All four v4.5 raw proposals sum to 0.965 and remain invalid.
Stage 4 claims the initial allocation already met the sum constraint despite three preceding calculator failures.
observed_local_failure.not_generalized: One reused development case, not evidence of population-level failure rates.

recommended_first_candidate.name: same_stage_budget_explicit_error_grounding_and_external_acceptance
recommended_first_candidate.change_scope: Make the current calculator failure and the instruction to revise the raw allocation explicit in the active task; derive acceptance status from a new calculator check, never from the model's self-approval.
recommended_first_candidate.controls: Retain four stages, model/decoding/time limits, source and market inputs, raw assistant history and feedback; add no extra generation attempts in this first candidate.
recommended_first_candidate.budget_evidence: Four stages is the existing LIBERA design, not the three outer attempts of Yang et al. or five code attempts of Arimbur. Preserving it limits a compute confound.
steps: Keep the prior raw proposal and its actual calculator result unchanged and visible.
Expose failing public task constraints, measured raw sum/residual and required existing condition in the current revision task; do not supply a corrected vector or a sector-specific suggested weight.
The model may change its own candidate. Preserve the new raw response, calculate it afresh and compare the old/new vectors without normalization.
Record changed versus unchanged, feasible versus infeasible and the truth of the model's feedback-use claim separately.
At the predeclared final opportunity, retain an invalid candidate as invalid; do not turn workflow completion into allocation success or continue unregistered retries.
recommended_first_candidate.early_stage_rule: An invalid provisional allocation is recorded and receives the next already-budgeted revision opportunity; it is never accepted as valid merely to advance the workflow.
recommended_first_candidate.no_guarantee: The v4.5 history already included calculator feedback. This narrower interface change is a testable hypothesis, not a literature-proven fix.

alternative_if_explicitly_selected_befor.name: bounded_candidate_revision_loop
alternative_if_explicitly_selected_befor.evidence: Yang et al. Appendix I Table 12; Arimbur Section V-H has the same total in a prompt ablation.
alternative_if_explicitly_selected_befor.warning: Candidate attempts must be defined separately from the four research stages; adding this loop changes call budget and protocol topology and cannot be attributed only to prompt grounding.

acceptance_and_terminal_rules.source_status: Explicit LIBERA engineering/measurement adaptation; no paper reports this exact contract.
acceptance_and_terminal_rules.numeric_acceptance: Only the existing complete finite 11-sector, long-only, full-investment calculator rules and existing tolerances; no target portfolio or new behavioral threshold.
acceptance_and_terminal_rules.numeric_tolerances: Existing implementation tolerances are not paper-derived behavioral parameters. Exact Decimal/Fraction residuals remain separately reported.
acceptance_and_terminal_rules.on_budget_exhausted: Preserve final raw invalid output, all failed checks and all attempts; status remains unresolved/invalid, with no successful-allocation claim.
acceptance_and_terminal_rules.on_timeout_or_incomplete_output: Preserve partial bytes and distinguish unobserved results from observed invalid complete proposals.
acceptance_and_terminal_rules.priority2_and_priority3: Do not begin until the three user-requested independent checks of priority 1 pass; three audits is a user instruction, not three model attempts or a paper-derived sample size.

falsifiable_outcomes: Did an invalid vector change after its actual failure feedback?
Did a new raw vector pass the unchanged calculator without repair?
Does the feedback-use claim agree with the actual prior and current results?
Did the run stop within its registered call/time budget and keep every failure?
claim_limits: Changing a candidate is not proof that feedback caused the change; this is a single development trajectory, not a randomized causal comparison.
A feasible allocation does not establish rationale faithfulness, financial optimality, realized return or model generality.
Mandatory acknowledgment alone has negative counterevidence; any status field is observational and must be checked against arithmetic.
No cited paper directly validates this frozen quantized 4B model on this 11-sector institutional-document task.
